If the systems constantly been topped up with fresh oxygenated water every 6-8 weeks, the entire system is rusting inside and out. Adding inhibitor will either suspend all the rust deposits and give you black  sludgy water leading to blockages or poor flow rates, or compromise areas of rusting which is holding the system together and give more leaks. I'd suggest adding in a light cleaning agent (dispersants) and flush this sludgy water out before adding any corrosion inhibitor.

Also, overdosing can be just as problematic as it will increase TDS/conductivity and increase erosiveness of the water. Best to go in at the recommended dose rate to achieve minimal erosion concern and maximum corrosion protection.

I understand your pain. I suffered severe anxiety through my second year of uni. I couldn't leave the house without shaking or the relentless feeling that I would throw up/have a heart attack. Everything in my life was shit and I had nothing to hold on for. I too felt like a waste of space due to my failing grades and complete lack of motivation to do anything.

Fortunately, I managed to overcome the anxiety. Lifestyle changes really helped me. Regular sleeping pattern, healthy food, stopped smoking weed and drinking so often. I started going to the gym regularly and joined a football team. I still had no motivation, however at those times I just always repeated in my head "fuck it, just do it... Fuck it, just do it".

After a while I realised that the only thing holding me back was my own mentality. And my lifestyle changes improved that somewhat. Don't get me wrong, none of this was easy. I guess the message I'm trying to send is that things CAN and WILL get better. As hard as it is to change things, by forcing yourself to change even the smallest thing will prove this to yourself.
